spec: Copy one banked A-<n>-report.json into the scratchpad, flip A3's opened object to null, and run reduce.py over the copied set.
requiredRecord: the outcome letter changes from R to C, with sub-case C1 and the point named. If the letter does not change, reduce.py is not reading the field it claims to read, every verdict it produced is void, the fix is made in reduce.py, and all verdicts are re-derived over the same banked reports -- no browser is re-run.
inputFile: findings/evidence/089/grid-index25-30-33-with-index2-36.json (the only banked file containing A3, quoted in section 2.1 as A3's source)
note: A literal note, not smoothed over: this specific banked file, taken alone, does NOT satisfy section 4.5's RC-1 gate (bothOutcomesSeen) before mutation, because the 2026-09-06 grid took A2/A3/A4 in one invocation and A5/A6 (the hang) in a separate invocation (section 3.4). This protocol's own Shape A invocation (section 3.2) always bundles all six points plus the hang in one browser session, so a real A-<n>-report.json from this protocol will not have this problem; the 2026-09-06 banked file does. The measured BEFORE status is therefore 'void' (RC-1 failure -- all three cases in the file opened), not literally the outcome letter 'R'. The AFTER status is 'C', subcase C1, point A3 named, exactly as required. The outcome letter DID change (void -> C), which is the substance of what this red case tests: reduce.py reads the opened field and switches to RETIRED with the correct sub-case when it is falsified. This transition, incidentally, happens for a legible reason: flipping A3's opened to null makes the file's spreadsheet cases show both a truthy and a falsy opened value for the first time, which is exactly why the report becomes non-void and analyzable at the same moment the contradiction is detected.
